title: Three-Week IB Psychology Revision Plan for November
summary: IB Psychology revision plan for November: triage topics, practise essays, use timed papers and protect rest across three flexible weeks for SL and HL.
body_markdown:
Three weeks before an IB examination session, the temptation is to treat every unfinished topic as equally urgent. It is not. A realistic **IB Psychology revision plan** should identify the knowledge most likely to cost you marks, repair those weaknesses through active recall and exam-style questions, then leave enough time for timed papers and recovery.


For students taking several November subjects, Psychology cannot occupy every evening. Nor should it. The aim is to complete focused sessions that improve recall, study selection and written analysis without destabilising the rest of your timetable.


One important detail comes first. Students sitting Psychology in November 2026 follow the course assessed before the new model begins in May 2027. That means preparation should reflect the biological, cognitive and sociocultural approaches in Paper 1, studied options in Paper 2, and research methods in Paper 3 for HL. If you are preparing for a later November session, confirm your syllabus with your coordinator and use RevisionDojo's guide to the[IB Psychology curriculum changes](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/ib-psychology-2025-curriculum-2027-changes) .


### Your three-week plan at a glance


Week Main objective Psychology priority Timed work


Week 1 Diagnose and rebuild Topic triage, core studies and command terms Short-answer responses and essay plans


Week 2 Convert knowledge into marks Full essays, evaluation and research methods Paper sections under time limits


Week 3 Rehearse and recover Error repair, selective recall and exam readiness Full papers in Exam mode


A useful weekly target is four Psychology sessions of 45-75 minutes, plus one longer timed session. Move them around your other examination dates. If another subject needs urgent attention, shorten a Psychology session rather than borrowing from sleep.


### Before week one, build a topic triage map


Spend your first 30 minutes creating three lists:


- **Secure:** you can explain the concept, select an appropriate study and answer without notes.
- **Unstable:** you recognise the content but struggle to retrieve details or evaluate evidence.
- **Missing:** you cannot currently construct a defensible response.


Test yourself before assigning a category. Recognition is deceptive because familiar notes can make weak knowledge feel strong. Close the book and write what you remember about a topic, including one relevant study, its procedure, findings and connection to the question.


The[RevisionDojo IB Psychology resource hub](https://www.revisiondojo.com/ib/ib-psychology-new) brings together Study Notes, Flashcards and Questionbank practice. Use the Questionbank for this first diagnosis. Three or four questions from different areas will reveal more than an hour of rereading.


Your triage should also account for likely return. A topic is high priority when it is weak, examinable and connected to several possible questions. A small factual gap in an otherwise secure topic deserves less time than an approach for which you cannot select or explain suitable research.


### Week one: rebuild recall and study selection


Week one is about making knowledge usable. Give each session one unstable or missing area rather than rotating through everything.


A practical session might look like this:


1. Retrieve the topic from memory for 10 minutes.
2. Check omissions using concise Study Notes.
3. Create or review Flashcards for definitions and study details.
4. Answer one short question without notes.
5. Record the error that most reduced your answer's quality.


Organise studies by argument, not merely by researcher name. For each one, know what it demonstrates, how the method supports or limits the conclusion, and which questions it can answer. A versatile study that you understand deeply is more useful than several studies memorised as disconnected summaries.


Command terms deserve their own attention. An answer that describes when the question asks you to evaluate can contain accurate psychology and still miss the task. Use the[IB exam command terms guide](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/ib-exam-command-terms-list) to distinguish instructions such as explain, discuss and evaluate.


Finish the week with three closed-book essay plans. Each plan should include a direct thesis, relevant evidence, explicit links to the prompt and balanced evaluation. Do not write every essay in full yet. Planning several responses develops range without consuming the time needed for your other subjects.


### Week two: turn knowledge into exam performance


Knowing a study and deploying it under pressure are different skills. Week two closes that gap.


Write at least two timed extended responses during the week. After each response, classify the problem rather than writing a vague note such as “revise more.” Was the weakness inaccurate recall, poor study selection, limited evaluation, weak structure or timing? RevisionDojo's AI Chat and Grading tools can help you inspect an answer, but feedback matters only when it produces a specific change in the next attempt.


For Paper 1, alternate between short-answer work and extended-response planning across the biological, cognitive and sociocultural approaches. For Paper 2, focus on the option or options taught by your school. HL students should also schedule two focused Paper 3 sessions covering research terminology, sampling, ethics, credibility and the interpretation of an unseen stimulus.


Use exam-style questions in clusters. Answering three questions on one weak topic makes patterns visible. Once accuracy improves, mix topics so that you must decide which knowledge applies. The[RevisionDojo Psychology coverage guide](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/revisiondojo-ib-psychology-coverage) explains how its question practice, notes and paper preparation fit together.


A student negotiates revision time with Psychology, Maths and Sleep seated as a tiny committee


Protect one evening from heavy revision. Rest is not a reward for finishing the syllabus. It is part of the plan that makes the following sessions usable.


### Week three: simulate, diagnose and taper


The final week should become narrower, not busier. You are no longer collecting everything you might know. You are rehearsing what you need to do.


Early in the week, sit a complete timed paper or the longest realistic section available. Use Questionbank material, Predicted Papers or Mock Exams, and complete the attempt in RevisionDojo's Exam mode. Keep notes closed, follow the correct time limit and continue when an answer feels imperfect. That discomfort is part of the rehearsal.


Review the attempt on the same day or the next morning. Divide errors into three groups:


- **Knowledge errors:** a concept or study could not be recalled accurately.
- **Application errors:** relevant knowledge was available but not connected to the question.
- **Execution errors:** structure, command terms or time management reduced the answer's quality.


Repair only the errors you found, then retest them with a fresh question. This simulate, diagnose, repair and retest cycle is more productive than immediately sitting another complete paper. The broader[IB exam-season study plan](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/ib-exam-season-study-plan) offers a useful framework when Psychology must share the week with five other subjects.


During the last 48 hours, reduce volume. Review study-purpose links, common evaluation points and your error log. If a concept remains confusing, ask AI Chat a precise question or work with one of RevisionDojo's Tutors rather than disappearing into an unfocused search.


Use the[realistic final-week guide](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/realistic-final-week-before-exams) to check sleep, travel, permitted equipment and examination times. Stop heavy work early enough to sleep normally. A final exhausted essay rarely compensates for a tired examination morning.


### Keep the plan flexible across several subjects


A timetable fails when it assumes every day will go perfectly. Build one floating session into each week. This can absorb unfinished Psychology work, move to another urgent subject or become rest if you remain on schedule.


On crowded days, use a minimum viable session: retrieve one study, answer one short question and update your error log. Twenty focused minutes preserves continuity. On lighter days, complete the longer writing and timed-paper work.


RevisionDojo works best as the central IB resource in this process because the workflow stays connected. Study Notes repair a gap, Flashcards test retrieval, the Questionbank turns knowledge into answers, and Grading tools expose the next improvement. Predicted Papers and Mock Exams then move that practice into realistic conditions.


Three weeks is not enough time to know everything perfectly. It is enough time to become more selective, more accurate and calmer about what the examination requires. Begin with honest triage, practise in the[IB Psychology Questionbank](https://www.revisiondojo.com/ib/ib-psychology-new) , and sit timed papers in Exam mode before November arrives.
